source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), conclusion appendix 2 and customs section
text:
Once a banana shipment is ready to leave Cambodia, it still has to clear Cambodian customs before export, using the ASYCUDA electronic customs system. In outline, this involves: the declarant (the exporter or their customs broker) lodging a Single Administrative Document (SAD) declaration electronically, after which the system automatically routes the declaration into one of several risk channels shown on the SAD form — commonly color-coded as red (requires full documentary check and physical goods inspection), yellow (documentary check only), green (automatic assessment with no physical check), or blue (post-clearance scrutiny/audit rather than inspection at the border). Declarations needing physical inspection go through a goods inspection step before customs re-routes them to "green" for release; once assessment is complete and any duties/fees are settled, a release order is printed and the goods are authorized to move.

Supporting paperwork typically bundled with a banana export shipment includes the commercial invoice, packing list, phytosanitary certificate, a list of containers, and a bill of trucking/lading — examples of all of these appear as sample filled-in documents in this guide's appendices, based on a real banana shipment from Kampong Cham province to Dalian, China via Vietnam.
